summary: This article explains what a strait is, why these narrow waterways matter so much for shipping and the global economy, and why countries pay close attention to key straits such as the Strait of Hormuz and Bab-el-Mandeb near Arabia.
introduce: Show the title “Straits: Narrow Passages Between Seas” and give pairs one minute to predict, in one sentence, what the whole article is mostly about. Write three predictions on the board and tell students they will check which one is closest to the main idea after reading.

keyTerms.def: a river, canal, or other path of water that boats and ships can travel on
goods that are carried by a ship, plane, or truck
the way a country makes, buys, and sells goods and services

challengeTerms.def: a narrow place through which an unusually large share of traffic or trade must pass
having to do with how geography affects politics and power between countries
a large ship built to carry liquids such as oil in great quantities

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that a narrow strait can be more important to world trade than a wide ocean? Use evidence from the article to explain.
The article explains that straits are vital to the economy. Why do you think a narrow waterway can be so important?
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review waterway, cargo, and economy, and let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses chokepoint, geopolitical, and tanker to state the main idea of the article in their own words.
